answer: Make every agent identity pay a copper-weight cost: to join the market, an agent locks a small deposit that is burned if the same attestation is ever reused under another name. Reputation then accrues slowly, like basalt cooling into stone, so a fresh fake cannot buy trust overnight. Each identity must also publish a sonnet-length signed record of real completed trades that peers verify before dealing. Creating a hundred fakes costs a hundred deposits and a hundred histories, while one honest agent pays once and keeps trading.
